item: Airplane mode refuses a plain http:// fetch through a loopback HTTP proxy before a byte reaches the proxy
summary: R619, from Steward 3's second security read of R616. A plain http:// URL fetched through an HTTP proxy (Privoxy chained to Tor, settings http_proxy) is written by urllib3 and by urllib.request as an absolute-form request line, GET http://host/x, to the loopback proxy socket, with no CONNECT. The socket guard saw only the allowed loopback connect and _tunnel is never called, so in airplane mode the proxy received the whole request and could forward it; live-reproduced with a loopback listener before the fix. src/ingest/airplane.py now also patches http.client.HTTPConnection.putrequest, the one call every http.client-based client hands its request target to before writing anything (urllib3 reaches it through super()), and guards the host an absolute-form target or a CONNECT authority names. Origin-form targets name only the connected peer and are left alone. An authority with userinfo, a backslash or whitespace, or an empty host, is treated as remote, because a proxy parsing it differently is the bypass itself. The new point joins _patch_points, the heal check, uninstall and the conftest leak check. Tests: a loopback listener receives zero bytes from requests and from urllib.request in airplane mode, receives the absolute-form GET online (the control), and receives it again with the putrequest patch removed (remove the guard, a test fails); unit cases for remote, loopback, IPv6, CONNECT and ambiguous targets. Stated limit: httpx/httpcore does not use http.client, so this patch point does not cover it; in this tree httpx is used only by the loopback-only LLM clients. Not touched: the https-through-a-loopback-proxy labelling issue (Export lane). Release-notes line: with airplane mode on, a plain http:// fetch through a local HTTP proxy is now refused before any byte reaches the proxy.
